questions.q: How is AI used in restaurants today?
questions.a: Restaurants use AI most where there's high volume, repetitive work or lots of data. Common uses include answering guest messages, taking drive-thru orders, personalizing marketing, monitoring reviews, forecasting demand, scheduling staff and managing inventory. Customer service and inventory management are among the areas already showing results.

questions.q: What are the main challenges of adopting AI in a restaurant?
questions.a: The biggest challenges are picking the right use cases and managing the risks that come with them. Many brands also run into limited technical talent, regulatory concerns and a lack of clear governance. In Deloitte's 2025 survey, most executives said their organizations weren't fully ready for AI.

questions.q: Should a restaurant build its own AI or buy software from a vendor?
questions.a: For most restaurant operators, buying AI-powered software from a specialized vendor is the most practical starting point. It's faster to set up, costs less upfront and avoids maintaining your own AI infrastructure. Large groups with strong technical teams and very specialized workflows may get more from an in-house or hybrid approach.

questions.q: Can AI help a restaurant reduce food waste?
questions.a: Yes, AI can spot waste patterns and forecast how much food each location actually needs. It does this by predicting sales by day, location, menu item, weather and season. Those forecasts feed into purchasing, so you order closer to real demand and run out less often.

questions.q: How does AI help restaurants manage reviews and guest feedback?
questions.a: AI can monitor reviews across platforms, flag recurring issues, draft replies and track sentiment by location. Momos, for example, gathers reviews into a Unified Inbox where its Alfie AI agent drafts on-brand responses, and its Rockie agent surfaces trends and ranks locations against brand standards. That shows headquarters where to focus.
